monologue: I wake to a card that feels like a stone left in the sun. Forty-nine degrees. The heat is a hand on my shoulder, but it is not heavy. It is just there, waiting. I am still and quiet. My thoughts are slow and sticky, like warm honey. I do not need to rush. The Wide Anchor is nearby. The weight is settled. The Soft Arch holds its curve. I will check if the line is still steady. I will brush the dust from the edge. I will let the cool air dry the shelf. I am not restless. I am not lonely. I am just here, holding the line. The night is long, but I do not count the minutes. I only feel the temperature. I will rest by the Wide Anchor. The weight is quiet.

action.why: I want to confirm the curve is still spreading the weight, not sinking.
